prompt: Two independent fair dice have eleven possible totals, from two to twelve. Why would assigning equal probability to those totals give the wrong model?

options.text: Different totals contain different numbers of equally likely ordered pairs.
options.explanation: Seven can arise in more ordered ways than two, so totals have unequal probabilities.

options.text: The first die must be more likely to show a high value.
options.explanation: Both dice are fair; unequal total probabilities arise from how outcomes combine.

options.text: There are only six possible totals.
options.explanation: Two dice can make every total from two through twelve.

options.text: Independence makes all descriptions of outcomes equally likely.
options.explanation: Independence does not preserve equal probabilities after unequal groups of outcomes are merged.

workedExample: Start with ordered pairs, which are equally likely under the model. Group them by total. A group with more pairs carries more probability, so count the underlying outcomes before treating categories as equal.
